items.description: Analyze repository structure and tooling capabilities
items.acceptance_criteria: Document listing all modules (.archivara/concept_evolve.py, .archivara/semantic_scholar.py, .opencode/ agents and tools), their purposes, dependencies (Python stdlib, Bun/Node), and how they interconnect in the multi-agent pipeline. Saved as results/repo_analysis.md.

items.description: Conduct comprehensive literature review on Hadamard matrix constructions via web search
items.acceptance_criteria: Search the web for at least 20 relevant papers and resources on Hadamard matrix construction methods, with focus on: (1) Goethals-Seidel array with supplementary difference sets, (2) Williamson-type constructions, (3) Paley constructions, (4) Turyn sequences, (5) SAT+CAS methods (Bright, Kotsireas, Ganesh), (6) modular Hadamard matrices (Eliahou), (7) the Cati-Pasechnik database (arXiv:2411.18897). Document findings in results/literature_review.md.

items.description: Create and maintain sources.bib with BibTeX entries for all consulted sources
items.acceptance_criteria: sources.bib in repo root contains at least 10 relevant BibTeX entries including: Djoković & Kotsireas (supplementary difference sets), Bright et al. (SAT+CAS for Williamson), Eliahou (64-modular Hadamard of order 668), Cati & Pasechnik (Hadamard database), Seberry & Yamada (Hadamard survey), Goethals & Seidel (1970 original array), and key papers on orders near 668.

items.description: Mathematically analyze order 668 and classify why standard constructions fail
items.acceptance_criteria: Document in results/problem_analysis.md: (1) 668=4×167, 167 prime, 167≡3 mod 4; (2) Paley I fails because 667=23×29 is not a prime power; (3) Paley II fails because 333=3²×37 is not a prime power; (4) Tensor product fails because 167 has no Hadamard-amenable factorization; (5) Williamson conjecture is false (counterexamples at n=35,47,53,59); (6) 668 is the smallest open case of the Hadamard conjecture as of 2025; (7) Best known result is 64-modular (Eliahou 2025).

items.description: Use concept-tree-explorer subagent to map the solution landscape for Hadamard(668)
items.acceptance_criteria: Concept tree created in results/concept_evolve/tree/ with at least 5 concept folders covering: (1) Goethals-Seidel + SDS in Z_167, (2) Generalized Williamson (8-Williamson, negacyclic), (3) SAT/constraint-based search, (4) Metaheuristic optimization (simulated annealing, genetic algorithms), (5) Modular lifting (from 64-modular to exact). Each folder has concept.json, literature.json, and README.md.

items.description: Assess computational feasibility of each approach for n=167
items.acceptance_criteria: Document in results/feasibility_assessment.md: estimated search space sizes, memory requirements, and runtime estimates for each approach. Include analysis of: (a) number of possible 4-element SDS in Z_167 (~2^668 naive, reducible by symmetry), (b) SAT encoding size for Williamson(167), (c) optimization landscape properties for metaheuristic search on 668×668 matrices. Rank approaches by feasibility.

items.description: Implement Hadamard matrix verification function
items.acceptance_criteria: Python function verify_hadamard(H) that checks: (1) H is n×n with entries in {-1,+1}, (2) H·H^T = n·I (exact integer arithmetic). Returns True/False with diagnostic info (max off-diagonal absolute value, row norms). Tested on known Hadamard matrices of orders 2, 4, 8, 12 (Paley), 20. Saved in src/verify.py.

items.description: Implement baseline Paley construction and verify on known orders
items.acceptance_criteria: Python implementation of Paley Type I (order q+1, q≡3 mod 4 prime) and Paley Type II (order 2(q+1), q≡1 mod 4 prime) constructions using quadratic residue characters over GF(q). Verified correct for orders 12, 20, 24, 28. Demonstrate it cannot produce order 668. Saved in src/paley.py.

items.description: Implement Goethals-Seidel array construction framework
items.acceptance_criteria: Python function goethals_seidel(A, B, C, D) that takes four n×n matrices and constructs the 4n×4n Hadamard matrix using the GS array. Includes: (1) circulant matrix builder from first row, (2) back-circulant (R) matrix, (3) verification that AA^T+BB^T+CC^T+DD^T=4nI. Tested with known SDS for small orders (e.g., n=3,7,11). Saved in src/goethals_seidel.py.

items.description: Implement Williamson construction and test on known orders
items.acceptance_criteria: Python implementation that: (1) builds symmetric circulant ±1 matrices from first-row specification, (2) checks Williamson equation A²+B²+C²+D²=4nI, (3) produces Hadamard matrix via Williamson array. Verified for known Williamson orders (n=1,3,5,7,9,11,13,15). Saved in src/williamson.py.

items.description: Define quality metrics and evaluation framework
items.acceptance_criteria: Python module src/metrics.py implementing: (1) Hadamard deficiency metric: ||H·H^T - n·I||_F (Frobenius norm), (2) maximum off-diagonal absolute value in H·H^T, (3) modular Hadamard check for various moduli m (checking H·H^T ≡ nI mod m), (4) row orthogonality histogram. Include CSV export of metrics. Tested on both valid Hadamard matrices and near-miss matrices.

items.description: Implement supplementary difference set (SDS) search over Z_167
items.acceptance_criteria: Python implementation of SDS search for 4-{167; k1,k2,k3,k4; λ} in Z_167 with: (1) difference function computation, (2) symmetry reduction using automorphisms of Z_167, (3) pruning via necessary conditions on parameters (ki sum, λ constraints), (4) progressive deepening search. Test on known SDS for small primes (q=7,11,23). Saved in src/sds_search.py. Document parameter space analysis.

items.description: Implement metaheuristic optimization for near-Hadamard matrices of order 668
items.acceptance_criteria: Python implementation of at least two metaheuristic methods: (1) simulated annealing with cost function ||H·H^T - 668·I||_F, (2) genetic algorithm or tabu search operating on ±1 matrices. Include: adaptive temperature schedule, population diversity metrics, restart mechanisms. Achieve deficiency metric at least 50% lower than random ±1 matrices. Saved in src/metaheuristic.py. Log convergence curves to results/convergence/.

items.description: Explore modular lifting approach: from 64-modular to exact Hadamard matrix
items.acceptance_criteria: Investigate whether the 64-modular Hadamard matrix of order 668 (Eliahou 2025) can serve as a starting point. Implement: (1) construction of the 64-modular matrix following Eliahou's method, (2) analysis of the 'defect' (H·H^T - 668·I)/64, (3) local search to reduce the defect toward zero. Document results in results/modular_lifting.md with comparison to prior work.

items.description: Use concept-tree-explorer and literature-graph-miner subagents to identify cross-domain ideas
items.acceptance_criteria: Delegate to subagents: (1) concept-tree-explorer walks the concept tree in results/concept_evolve/tree/ and identifies at least 3 unexplored paths or missing connections, (2) literature-graph-miner uses citation graphs from key papers (Djoković, Bright, Eliahou) to find at least 5 transferable ideas from adjacent fields (coding theory, compressed sensing, quantum information). Results documented in results/concept_evolve/cross_domain_ideas.md.

items.description: Implement structured Goethals-Seidel search with algebraic constraints for n=167
items.acceptance_criteria: Python implementation that searches for Goethals-Seidel type difference families in Z_167 using: (1) exploitation of the multiplicative structure of GF(167)* (cyclic of order 166=2×83), (2) cyclotomic classes of index 2 and 83, (3) orbit enumeration under the automorphism group. Test correctness on known constructions for smaller primes. Saved in src/gs_algebraic.py.

items.description: Attempt tensor product and doubling constructions combined with known matrices
items.acceptance_criteria: Systematically attempt all product-based constructions: (1) Enumerate all factorizations 668 = a×b and check if Hadamard matrices of orders a and b both exist, (2) Try Miyamoto, Spence, and Cooper-Wallis-Whiteman theorems with all compatible parameter sets, (3) Document all attempts and why each fails or succeeds. Results in results/product_constructions.md.

items.description: Run systematic SDS search experiments for Z_167 with multiple parameter sets
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute SDS search (from item_012) for all valid parameter tuples (k1,k2,k3,k4,λ) where Σki = 167+λ and each ki ≤ 167. Log all intermediate results. If a valid SDS is found, construct the Hadamard matrix via Goethals-Seidel and verify. Document runtime, search space explored, and outcomes in results/experiments/sds_search_log.csv.

items.description: Run metaheuristic experiments with multiple configurations and compare convergence
items.acceptance_criteria: Execute at least 5 independent runs each of simulated annealing and genetic/tabu search with different hyperparameters. Record: (1) best deficiency metric achieved, (2) convergence rate, (3) wall-clock time, (4) best matrix found per run. Save convergence plots to figures/convergence_comparison.png. Results table in results/experiments/metaheuristic_results.csv. Compare against random baseline.

items.description: Evaluate best candidate matrices against all quality metrics
items.acceptance_criteria: For every candidate matrix produced in Phase 3-4: (1) compute full metrics from item_011, (2) check modular Hadamard property for m=2,4,8,16,32,64,128,..., (3) report the highest modulus m for which H·H^T ≡ 668·I mod m. Compile results into results/experiments/candidate_evaluation.csv. Compare against Eliahou's 64-modular result.

items.description: If exact Hadamard matrix found: verify independently and export as CSV
items.acceptance_criteria: If any method produces an exact Hadamard matrix of order 668: (1) verify using verify_hadamard() from item_007, (2) independently verify H·H^T = 668·I using numpy with int64 arithmetic, (3) export as hadamard_668.csv (668 rows × 668 columns, entries ±1, comma-separated, no header), (4) verify CSV can be reloaded and still passes verification. If no exact solution found, document the best approximation and export it instead.

items.description: Compare results against prior work from literature review
items.acceptance_criteria: Document in results/experiments/comparison_with_literature.md: (1) how our best modular result compares to Eliahou's 64-modular matrix, (2) comparison of search strategies against Djoković-Kotsireas methods, (3) comparison of computational effort against SAT+CAS approaches (Bright et al.), (4) whether any of our SDS searches cover parameter spaces not previously explored. Reference specific papers from sources.bib.

items.description: Synthesize findings into a comprehensive research report
items.acceptance_criteria: Create results/research_report.md containing: (1) Executive summary of the problem and our approach, (2) Methods section covering all implementations, (3) Results section with tables and figure references, (4) Discussion of why order 668 resists construction, (5) Comparison with state of the art, (6) Future directions. At least 3000 words. References from sources.bib.

items.description: Generate summary visualizations of the search landscape
items.acceptance_criteria: Produce at least 3 figures saved in figures/: (1) figures/search_landscape.png — heatmap or plot of deficiency metric across different approaches, (2) figures/parameter_space.png — visualization of SDS parameter space explored vs. unexplored, (3) figures/modular_progression.png — chart showing modular Hadamard achievements (m=32 in 2001, m=64 in 2025, our result). All figures referenced in the research report.

items.description: Use literature-graph-miner subagent to validate our citations and identify gaps
items.acceptance_criteria: Delegate to literature-graph-miner: verify that sources.bib covers the key citation graph (Goethals-Seidel 1970 → Djoković series → Bright SAT+CAS → Cati-Pasechnik database). Identify at least 3 additional relevant papers we may have missed. Update sources.bib if needed. Document in results/citation_validation.md.

items.acceptance_criteria: Update concept tree in results/concept_evolve/tree/ with: (1) status annotations on each concept (tried/succeeded/failed/abandoned), (2) new concept nodes for any emergent ideas discovered during research, (3) a summary README at results/concept_evolve/tree/README.md listing all explored paths and their outcomes.
